competitions.title: HackSprint 2026: Campus AI & Sustainability
competitions.tagline: Build generative AI and IoT solutions tackling green campus challenges.
competitions.description: HackSprint 2026 is the annual flagship 36-hour hackathon connecting passionate engineering students with industry mentors. Develop real-world applications combining multimodal AI, energy conservation, smart waste sorting, or smart campus mobility.
competitions.rules:
1. All code must be authored during the hackathon.
2. Open-source libraries and generative AI tools are permitted with proper attribution.
3. Teams must consist of 2 to 4 registered college students.
4. Submissions must include GitHub repository and working demo video.

rounds.description: Submit functional GitHub repository, deployed demo link, and a 2-minute walkthrough video.

rounds.title: Round 3: Grand Finale Live Pitch
rounds.description: Top 5 shortlisted squads pitch live before the industry judging panel.

submissions.projectTitle: EcoCampus AI: Smart Energy & Waste Dispatcher
submissions.abstract: An autonomous IoT & vision pipeline that monitors energy waste across campus auditoriums, predicts HVAC surge loads using LSTM models, and classifies bin recyclables with Edge AI.

comments.text: The LSTM load prediction accuracy on historical campus data is remarkably solid. Great work on the real-time websocket feed!
Love the clean React UI! Did you test the bin classification camera under low-light conditions?
Tested the live demo on mobile browser. The responsive dashboard renders beautifully and the WebSocket alert is instant!

submissions.abstract: Micro-grid solar production forecaster utilizing real-time campus weather station feeds and cloud tracking sensors to optimize battery charging schedules.

comments.text: Impressive InfluxDB time-series ingestion speed! Are the solar irradiance forecasts updated hourly or continuously?

submissions.abstract: Low-power LoRaWAN mesh nodes measuring indoor air quality, temperature, and occupancy with solar harvesting.
Indoor navigation quadcopter swarm equipped with lidar and thermal vision to map collapsed structures without GPS.

comments.text: Thrilled to see the optical flow localization working without GPS indoors. Safety netting in Arena C is ready for your team demo.

submissions.summary: Solved CC-101 in JAVASCRIPT with 5/5 tests passed.
Quiz completed: 2/10 correct. Gross Score: 188 pts (Accuracy: 20%).

evaluations.privateFeedback: Very strong architecture. The Edge AI inference on the low-cost Raspberry Pi node was particularly convincing.
evaluations.publicFeedback: Superb end-to-end prototype with clean React interface and impressive real-world energy saving metric projections.

evaluations.privateFeedback: Good time-series model. Might struggle under sudden unpredicted micro-climate cloud coverage.
evaluations.publicFeedback: Great concept and practical use of micro-grid solar prediction. UI could use more intuitive charts.

evaluations.privateFeedback: Exceptional mechanical and sensor integration. The SLAM algorithm recovered remarkably well when light levels dropped.
evaluations.publicFeedback: World-class hardware demo. The real-time 3D point cloud generation was seamless.

evaluations.feedback: Automated Arena Judge: ACCEPTED. Execution completed in 6ms.
Live Buzzer Arena Result: Accuracy 20%, Streak 2x, Score 24/100.

tickets.subject: Edge ML Model Quantization & PyTorch ONNX Runtime on Raspberry Pi
tickets.description: We are observing high inferencing latency (over 450ms) when running our YOLOv8 nano model on the edge device. Would like advice on INT8 quantization and hardware acceleration.

responses.message: Export your model using opset=17 and use the onnxruntime-openvino or NCNN backend. You can also apply dynamic post-training quantization to reduce weights from FP32 to INT8, achieving ~65ms inference on Cortex-A72 cores.

tickets.subject: Request for ACS712 Current Sensor and ESP32 Dev Board
tickets.description: Our team needs two ACS712 30A current sensor modules and one spare ESP32 NodeMCU board for monitoring solar panel micro-inverter power fluctuations.

responses.message: Components have been allocated and kept at the Hardware Distribution Booth in Lab 204. Please collect them with your Team Lead ID card.

tickets.subject: Clarification on Live Autonomous Flight Test Area
tickets.description: For Round 2 Jury Deliberation, can our drone fly autonomously indoors with optical flow sensors, or is safety netting mandatory around the flight arena?

responses.message: Safety netting is mandatory for any indoor flight above 1 meter altitude. Arena C in the sports complex is fully netted and will be assigned for your demo slot.

tickets.subject: Request for LoRaWAN gateway frequency configuration
tickets.description: Our squad NeuralKnights requires the EU868 vs IN865 band settings for the campus greenhouse gateway.

responses.message: Greenhouse gateway operates on 865-867 MHz band. Lab kit documentation has been placed in Innovation Lab 204.
